candidates.old:
.list_recorded
{
    TXA                             \ X = ren_i on entry (the one caller)
    LDX list_n
    STA list_slot,X
    LDA rec_type,Y
    AND #&7F
    STA list_type
    LDA rec_wxl,Y                   \ where it was drawn (BUGS #7)
    STA list_x_lo
    LDA rec_wxh,Y
    STA list_x_hi
    LDA rec_wy,Y
    JMP list_finish
}
candidates.new:
.list_recorded
{
    TXA                             \ X = ren_i on entry (the one caller)
    LDX list_n
    STA list_slot,X
    LDA rec_wxl,Y                   \ where it was drawn (BUGS #7)
    STA list_x_lo                   \ (x2's, once the type has taken Y)
    SEC                             \ x1 = x - 1
    SBC #1
    STA list_x1_lo,X
    LDA rec_wxh,Y
    STA list_x_hi
    SBC #0
    STA list_x1_hi,X
    LDA rec_type,Y
    AND #&7F
    TAX                             \ X = type: list_finish's work, here, with n in Y
    LDA rec_wy,Y
    LDY list_n
    SEC                             \ y1 = y - 2 (or 0)
    SBC #2
    BCC lrec_low
    STA list_y1,Y
    ADC mover_types_height_table,X  \ C set: y - 2 + height + 1
    BCS lrec_top
    ADC #3                          \ y2 = y + height + 2 (or &FF)
    BCS lrec_top
.lrec_y2
    STA list_y2,Y
    LDA list_x_lo                   \ x2 = x + width + 1
    SEC
    ADC mover_types_width_table,X
    STA list_x2_lo,Y
    LDA list_x_hi
    ADC #0
    STA list_x2_hi,Y
    RTS
.lrec_top
    LDA #&FF
    BRA lrec_y2                     \ 65C02 opcode
.lrec_low                           \ y < 2 (A = y - 2 + 256, C clear): list_finish's, from the top
    ADC #2                          \ A = y
    STX list_type
    LDX list_n
    JMP list_finish
}
candidates.summary: list_recorded does list_finish's work itself with the registers swapped (X = type, Y = list_n): x1 is computed from the loaded x with no trip through list_x_lo/hi, the type goes TAX instead of a store and a reload, and the JMP list_finish goes. y<2 (never in the profile) re-enters list_finish from the top. Measured on a scratch bench build (1500 passes seed 1, pcprof): list_finish -200, list_recorded +178 a pass, whole work -31 a pass; passlock seed 1 3000 passes and seed 3 4000 passes identical (state and screen), helilock 5 identical.
candidates.equivalence: Outputs identical: list_slot[n] = ren_i; x1 = x - 1 and x2 = x + width + 1 (16-bit, same SEC/SBC#1/SBC#0 and SEC/ADC width/ADC#0 chains); y1 = max(y - 2, 0) and y2 = min(y + height + 2, 255) by the same ADC chain (carry out of y - 2 + h + 1 or of + 3 gives &FF at lrec_top, which stores A=&FF through the common store). y < 2 (BCC): ADC #2 restores A = y (C was clear, so y + 254 + 2 sets C) and list_type, X = list_n are set for a JMP list_finish that redoes every store identically. Checked with an instruction-level model of old and new over 300,000 random cases (y in 0,1,2,3,254,255 and random, heights 0-255, x_lo 0/1/255, x_hi 0/1/255, type bit 7 set or clear, any n, any slot): the seven arrays equal in all. list_type, list_x_lo, list_x_hi are read only by list_finish (grep across src/, tools/): list_recorded no longer leaves list_type, and leaves list_x_lo/hi = x (as before); both are rewritten by list_live before any other read. The one caller does LDX ren_i; BIT need,X after, so A, X, Y, flags on return are free. Interrupt: ren_zp bytes are not touched by it.
candidates.relies_on: Page crossings: grows the code after it by 59 bytes (list_finish &98A5 -> &98E0, widen_by_live &98EE -> &9929, list_overlap &9948 -> &9983); list_finish and widen_by_live both straddle &9900 in this build (no hot branch in list_finish crosses: its BCC y2_ok is no longer on the hot path here, the new code falls through). Downstream layout noise measured at +/-5 cycles a pass in the profile (draw_column -3), the direct saving was -22 (list_finish -200, list_recorded +178 over 1500 passes). Relies on list_finish keeping its contract (A = y, X = list_n, list_type/list_x_lo/hi) for the lrec_low re-entry, and on list_recorded's single caller (close_over_overlaps) having ren_i in zero page and Y = ren_i + boff. Uses abs,Y stores (STA list_y1,Y, list_y2,Y, list_x2_lo,Y, list_x2_hi,Y: all absolute, no zero-page,Y form needed) and abs,X reads of the two type tables (same page-crossing penalty as ,Y: same index value). Needs list_n < 255 (it is < &22).

candidates.new:
.next_a
    INX                             \ each_a, here: the loop's tail without its BRA
    CPX list_n
    BEQ swept
    LDY list_slot,X
    LDA need,Y
    BNE next_a                      \ already coming off or going on
    LDY #0
    BRA each_b                      \ 65C02 opcode
candidates.summary: next_a (hit 2.6 times a pass, 2.1 of them straight round again because the slot's need is already set) carries each_a's head inline, so the loop tail has no BRA each_a; the one path that goes on to each_b (0.5 a pass) takes a BRA each_b instead of falling through. Measured alone on a scratch bench build: render -11 a pass (of which about 6.4 is this, the rest layout).
candidates.equivalence: Instruction-for-instruction the same as INX; BRA each_a; each_a: CPX list_n; BEQ swept; LDY list_slot,X; LDA need,Y; BNE next_a; LDY #0; fall into each_b. The copy ends BRA each_b with A, X, Y, flags the same as the fall-through. each_a stays for the 'again' entry. No other label moves meaning; next_a keeps its address as the first byte of the copy.
candidates.relies_on: Page crossings: grows close_over_overlaps by 14 bytes (list_recorded &9862 -> &9870, everything downstream +14); all of next_a, swept and the loop's branches stay within page &98 (BNE next_a from each_a, BEQ swept, BEQ next_a from each_b). Measured: render -11 a pass alone, -1 a pass on top of candidate A (layout noise of about +/-5 on the downstream draw code, which the gate decides). Does not touch what any other label points at.

candidates.old:
.next_b
    LDY list_b
    INY
    BRA each_b                      \ 65C02 opcode
candidates.new:
.next_b
    LDY list_b                      \ each_b, here: the loop's tail without its BRA
    INY
    CPY list_n
    BEQ next_a
    STY list_b
    LDA list_slot,Y
    TAY
    LDA need,Y
    BEQ next_b                      \ staying too: no reason
    TYA
    BEQ next_b
    CMP list_slot,X
    BCC below
    LDY list_slot,X
    BNE next_b
    BRA below                       \ 65C02 opcode
candidates.summary: next_b (1.6 a pass) carries each_b's head and the rest of its body inline (the final BRA below instead of falling into .below), so the b loop's tail has no BRA each_b. Measured alone: render -16 a pass (4.7 is this).
candidates.equivalence: A copy of each_b's body from CPY list_n through BNE next_b, entered with Y = list_b + 1 exactly as each_b is (INY then CPY). Paths: CPY=list_n -> BEQ next_a (same); need,Y = 0 -> next_b (the copy, the same loop); b = player (TYA/BEQ) -> next_b; CMP/BCC -> below; LDY list_slot,X / BNE next_b; else BRA below (the original falls into .below). Registers and flags at .below, next_a and next_b are as in the original on each path. each_b stays for the first entry (LDY #0 from each_a and from next_a's copy).
candidates.relies_on: Page crossings: grows by 28 bytes (+14 with B1). All branches in the copy are within page &98; the BRA below is a backward branch of about 50 bytes inside close_over_overlaps. Alternative to nothing; independent of A, B1, L but their sizes add to the downstream shift (A+B1+B2+L: list_finish &98A5 -> &9909, measured render -27 a pass in all, against -31 for A alone: layout of draw_column +11). Refers to .below, .next_a, .next_b, list_b, list_slot, need as they are.

candidates.new:
.list_live
{
    TXA                             \ X = ren_i on entry (both callers)
    TAY
    LDX list_n
    STA list_slot,X
    STY dm_slot                     \ world_of_address's slot (BUGS #10); put_on sets its own
candidates.summary: list_live: both callers (going_on, widen_by_live) have X = ren_i, so TXA; TAY replaces LDY ren_i; TYA, one cycle and one byte fewer (the store of dm_slot still takes Y).
candidates.equivalence: Same values: A = Y = ren_i, X = list_n at the STA list_slot,X, dm_slot = ren_i, then unchanged. The old code read ren_i from zero page; at both call sites X = ren_i: close_over_overlaps' going_on follows LDX act,Y; STX ren_i ... LDA need,X (X untouched) ; widen_by_live follows LDX ren_i, BIT need,X, and its LDA/PHA/LDA/STA do not touch X.
candidates.relies_on: Relies on every caller of list_live having X = ren_i (grep: only the JSR at going_on and the JSR in widen_by_live; no entry past the label). Moves everything after by -1 byte (list_finish &98A5 -> &98A4); measured render -2 a pass alone.
